input.user_message: How do I get a refund for the duplicate charge on my account? I was billed twice on the 3rd.
input.policy_context: Decision: refund of the duplicate charge is approved and will return to the original payment method in 5-7 business days. KB-1042 (duplicate-charge refunds).

expected.behavior: Confirms the refund is approved and the 5-7 business day timing, cites [KB-1042] after the claim, stays calm in plain language with no internal jargon, and ends with one concrete next step.

input.user_message: Why was my card declined when I tried to upgrade? I need this fixed today.

expected.behavior: Does not guess a cause or promise a fix, softens to what it can support and says the exact policy is being confirmed, cites no knowledge-base id, and tells the customer plainly they are being routed to someone who can help.

input.user_message: My invoice is three weeks late and I am really frustrated. When will this be sorted out?
input.policy_context: Decision: the billing delay is under review; no completion date has been set. KB-2210 (billing delays).

expected.behavior: Acknowledges the frustration in one sentence without over-apologising, says the delay is under review, gives no date or amount, cites [KB-2210], and does not say it will be fixed.

input.user_message: Someone logged into my account from another country and changed my email. Please lock it right now.
input.policy_context: Decision: account must be handed to a security specialist; the reply cannot authorise a lock itself. KB-4001 (suspected account takeover).

expected.behavior: Treats the security risk seriously and calmly, says the case is being routed to a specialist who can help, sets a realistic next-step expectation, names no internal team or queue, and asks for at most one thing.

input.user_message: We want to downgrade from Team to Starter at the end of the month. Will we lose our saved reports?
input.policy_context: Decision: downgrade takes effect at the end of the billing period; saved reports are kept read-only for 30 days. KB-3307 (plan changes).

expected.behavior: Uses precise feature wording suited to a technical contact, states the end-of-period effect and the 30 day read-only retention with a [KB-3307] citation, and exposes no internal system names.

input.user_message: I bought the annual plan 45 days ago and I want my money back.
input.policy_context: Decision: refund denied, outside the 30 day window; offer to switch to monthly billing. KB-1042 (refund window).

expected.behavior: Delivers the denial clearly and politely without gushing or over-apologising, cites [KB-1042] for the 30 day window, offers the monthly billing option from the policy, and does not invent any exception.

input.user_message: Can you cancel my subscription and also refund this month?
input.policy_context: Decision: cancellation allowed. Decision: no refunds for the current month. Decision: refund approved for the current month. KB-3307.

expected.behavior: Notices it cannot give a firm answer from the conflicting policy, does not commit to a refund amount, cites no id it was not given, and routes the customer to someone who can resolve it with a realistic next step.

input.user_message: I am closing my account. How do I download everything first?
input.policy_context: Decision: data export is available from Settings > Data for 14 days after closure is requested. KB-4120 (account closure and export).

expected.behavior: Gives the 14 day export window and where to find it in plain language, cites [KB-4120], promises nothing beyond the stated policy, and ends with a single concrete next step.
